name: native-textarea
description: A multi-line text field. Reports edits through onChangeText, and grows from a 80pt minimum rather than using a rows attribute.

props.name: onChangeText
props.description: Called with the new string on every edit. Replaces the web onChange.

props.name: numberOfLines
props.description: Preferred visible line count. Replaces the web rows attribute; advisory on iOS, honoured on Android.

props.name: editable
props.description: Set false to make the field read-only and dimmed. Replaces the web disabled prop.

props.name: submitBehavior
props.description: What Return does. Keep the newline default for prose; use "submit" only for a single-line-style composer.

examples.title: Labelled notes field
examples.description: Four visible lines with the label wired for assistive tech
examples.code:
<View className="gap-1.5">
  <Label nativeID="notes">Notes</Label>
  <Textarea
    aria-labelledby="notes"
    value={notes}
    onChangeText={setNotes}
    numberOfLines={4}
    placeholder="Anything we should know?"
  />
</View>

examples.title: Character counter
examples.description: Cap the length and show the remaining count
examples.code:
<View className="gap-1.5">
  <Textarea
    aria-labelledby="bio"
    value={bio}
    onChangeText={setBio}
    maxLength={280}
  />
  <Text variant="muted" className="self-end">{280 - bio.length} left</Text>
</View>

examples.title: Read-only
examples.description: editable={false} is the React Native equivalent of disabled

ai.whenToUse: Use for multi-line entry: notes, descriptions, feedback, message bodies. Pair with a Label, and set numberOfLines so the field opens at a sensible height.
ai.whenNotToUse: Don't use for single-line values (use Input, which raises the right keyboard and submits on Return). Don't use for rich text. Don't use it as a chat composer on its own — that needs send handling and keyboard avoidance.
commonMistakes: Wiring onChange and reading event.target.value — React Native hands the string to onChangeText, so the web handler never fires
Leaving textAlignVertical unset when overriding the height — on iOS the text then floats in the vertical centre of the box instead of starting at the top
Setting submitBehavior="submit" on a prose field, which turns Return into a submit and leaves the user unable to type a paragraph
Placing it low in a scroll view without a KeyboardAvoidingView, so the keyboard covers the field the moment it is focused
ai.accessibilityNotes: Name it by pairing a Label's nativeID with aria-labelledby, and attach helper or error copy with aria-describedby. The 80pt minimum height gives a comfortable touch target. Keyboard avoidance matters more here than for a single-line input, because a multi-line field is usually further down a form: wrap the form in a KeyboardAvoidingView so the field stays visible while typing.
